solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: People's food likes oddly exposed

definitions.note: the 's is read as 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of food likes lays them bare while the even ones stay covered

explanation.surface: A diner's favourite dishes are revealed in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly exposed' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'food likes'. 'People's' is People plus 's read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Folks is an informal plural word for people in general.

clue.text: Sudden vivid memory of, say, Gordon Champion

parts.note: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero, so Gordon, say, suggests his first name
to back is to champion or support

explanation.surface: A sudden memory of someone named Gordon who was a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Champion' looks like a person's name. FLASH comes from Flash Gordon, the comic-strip space hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashback is an abrupt, vivid recollection of a past event, especially a traumatic one.

clue.text: Did spring article in Paris: fitting!

parts.note: le is a French definite article
fitting means apt, suitable

explanation.surface: A Paris newspaper piece published in spring was appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump, and its past tense is a synonym of jumped.

clue.text: Corruption of niece's MP, for example

indicators.note: corruption of means the letters of niece's MP are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of parliament corrupting his niece is a typical case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corruption of' rearranges NIECES MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example or sample of a type, so it stands for the phrase as a noun.

clue.text: June's last tango: it hit her badly

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: badly says the letters of it hit her are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A dance on the last day of June knocks a woman over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IT HIT HER into HIRTIETH, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: June has thirty days, so its final day is the thirtieth of the month.

clue.text: Row concerning whose turn it is to catch up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in tag and similar games the player whose turn it is to chase is called it

explanation.surface: An argument over whose turn it is to chase the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch up' reverses RE + IT. 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line, as in theatre seating.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows, such as raised seating in a stadium.

clue.text: Those who investigate report of tavern ghosts?

indicators.note: report of means what follows is what is heard spoken

parts.note: a tavern is an inn and ghosts are spectres

explanation.surface: Investigators look into stories of a haunted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' signals a homophone: INN SPECTRES spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors examine and look into matters, and police inspectors are detectives.

clue.text: Excellent advice to papa

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Great guidance for a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Lover once wholly transfixed by island of great beauty

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: transfixed by means pierced through, so the island goes into the middle

parts.note: quite means completely, wholly

explanation.surface: A former lover was utterly captivated by a gorgeous island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfixed by' means pierced, so the island sits in the middle of the word for wholly.
explanation.definitionFit: Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful and delicate.

clue.text: Scavenger has briefly to contain hunger

indicators.note: to contain says the shortened word holds the craving inside
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of has goes

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short
a yen is a craving or hunger

explanation.surface: A scavenging creature must keep its hunger in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of has; 'to contain' wraps that around the craving, the Japanese currency's other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are African carnivores well known for feeding on carcasses left by other predators.

clue.text: Grasp a fighting European by the head

parts.note: fighting is war
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours and place names such as Sheerness

explanation.surface: A warring European seizes someone by the head.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, a common element of British coastal place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp of something is an understanding or knowledge of it, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Card player's score put out?

definitions.meaning: in the card game piquet, scoring thirty points before the opponent scores is this bonus
put out means annoyed or resentful, as in a fit of offended pride

explanation.surface: A card player's tally might be thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: In piquet the bonus for reaching thirty first is called this; separately it is wounded pride or irritation.

clue.text: I'm sharp, but would I ever make a fast bowler?

definitions.text: I'm sharp, but would I ever make a fast bowler?

parts.words: I'm sharp, but would I ever make a fast bowler?
parts.note: a pointed object that fastens a bowler, a hard round hat, to the head; the surface is about pace bowling in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: A 'fast bowler' sounds like cricket's quick bowler, but here a bowler is a hat and 'fast' means secured.
explanation.definitionFit: The long pin used to hold a hat in place is sharp and fastens a bowler hat.

clue.text: Bloomer I committed originally in city of star-crossed lovers

indicators.note: in says the letters before it go inside the city's name

parts.note: Verona is the setting of Romeo and Juliet, the star-crossed lovers

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of committed is used

explanation.surface: Someone admits a blunder made in Verona, Romeo and Juliet's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, or speedwell, is a flowering plant, and a bloomer is something that flowers.

clue.text: Quickly, singer grabs large wader

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds, so the singer word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
an egret is a wading bird, a kind of heron

explanation.surface: A singer swiftly seizes a big wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly' is a music marking: allegretto is a tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical direction for a fairly brisk tempo, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Battle had around American, 50, in posh hotel

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: had, as in had a meal, is ate

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the hotel's name

parts.note: the Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A wartime tale of an American turning fifty at a luxury hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' and 'in' each signal a container. 'had' is read as consumed, as in had dinner; the Ritz is the luxury London hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerlitz, in 1805, was Napoleon's great victory over Russia and Austria.

clue.text: Survivor of The Archers broadcast absent as ISIHAC's beginning

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
beginning takes just the opening letter of ISIHAC

explanation.surface: A long-running radio soap's cast member is missing, like one from a radio comedy panel game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a BBC radio soap, ISIHAC the radio comedy show I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue; here the archers are those who shot the saint. 'broadcast' rearranges ABSENT AS + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Sebastian was shot with arrows by archers yet survived, before later being martyred.

clue.text: Request one's placed between wife and husband

indicators.note: placed between says the piece sits inside, between the two letters on either side

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, giving IS

explanation.surface: A request that one person be seated between a married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: W and H are the genealogical abbreviations for wife and husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish is a desire expressed, so the noun can stand for a request.

clue.text: Initially has sort of connection with railway's sound management

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of has is taken

parts.note: USB is a type of computer connection port
with means along with, and
RY is short for railway; the 's is a link word

explanation.surface: A railway with a certain kind of link is said to be well run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like noise; here it means prudent.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry means careful, economical management of resources, as well as farming.

clue.text: Six huge guards left keeping watch

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: guards means encloses protectively, so the huge word surrounds the letter for left

parts.note: giant means huge

explanation.surface: Six enormous sentries stay alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' puts L inside GIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilant means watchful and alert to danger, the state of someone keeping watch.

clue.text: Port contributing to high-risk obesity

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Drinking port is one cause of dangerous weight gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Kobe is a major Japanese seaport city on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Quality of fine champers, maybe, or Pilsener, as drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters reeling about, so Pilsener as is rearranged

explanation.surface: Sparkling wine or lager may have a fine quality when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PILSENER AS. Champers is British slang for champagne; its fine bubbles look like little pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne bubbles are often likened to pearls, so its quality of fine bubbles is a pearl-like character.

clue.text: Like the Dutch, prudently changing shillings to francs

indicators.note: changing one thing for another signals swapping the shillings letter out of the prudent word
to names what the shillings letter is changed into, the letter for francs

parts.note: acting prudently is acting wisely
S is the abbreviation for shillings, from the Latin solidus
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: Like the thrifty Dutch, switching shillings for francs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old Dutch', not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Wifely means characteristic of a wife, and Dutch is old London slang for one's spouse.

clue.text: Prime journal, not the first treatise on animals

parts.note: prime means best, of top quality

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the journal word is dropped

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: A top-quality periodical, not the original, carries a study of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the D of DIARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestiary is a medieval book describing real and fabulous beasts, often with moral lessons.

clue.text: Branch to yield to auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to bow is to yield or submit

explanation.surface: A company branch must give way to the accountants checking its books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' looks like accountants; here it means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bough is a large branch of a tree.

clue.text: After battle, Napoleon evacuated a part of Austria

parts.note: to vie is to contend or battle

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters of Napoleon remain

explanation.surface: After a battle, Napoleon withdrew from a region of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties Napoleon to NN. The surface recalls Napoleon's occupations of Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is Austria's capital and one of its federal states.

clue.text: Celebrated day school being over

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A well-known day school has closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being over' reverses D + ETON. Eton is England's best-known private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means famous or well known, a synonym of celebrated as an adjective.

clue.text: No place for Scott or Janis to wed

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letters for place are removed

parts.note: Scott Joplin, the ragtime composer, and Janis Joplin, the rock singer, share a surname
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Neither Scott nor Janis has anywhere to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No place' removes PL from JOPLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to unite or link together, as in joining two people in marriage.

clue.text: Marry supporter of international organisation?

definitions.meaning: to marry is to join two people together
a whimsical coinage: a follower of the UN would be a ..., like a Luddite

explanation.surface: Wed a backer of a global body.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up word, UN plus -ITE, the suffix for a follower, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniting two people in wedlock is to marry them; the coinage names a supporter of the United Nations.

clue.text: Sampled bottles without means, at first, such as schooners?

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the sampling word contains the other pieces

parts.note: to sample food or drink is to taste it
w/o is the written abbreviation for without

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of means

explanation.surface: A wine taster with no money sampled schooners, which are also sherry glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' signals a container; w/o is the written shorthand for without. A schooner is also a large sherry glass, feeding the drinking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooners are sailing ships typically rigged with two masts, so they are examples; the question mark flags this.

clue.text: Fine-tune variable way of working on holiday

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or perfect
Y is a typical algebraic variable
MO is modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: Adjusting a flexible working method while away on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for modus operandi; algebra's unknowns X, Y, Z give Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday a newly married couple takes after the wedding.

clue.text: Current age of US lawman given in play

indicators.note: given in says the lawman is put inside the play word

parts.note: to toy is to play with something
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: How old an American lawyer is, as stated in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in' signals a container; 'age' looks like a number of years, but the definition is the present era.
explanation.definitionFit: Today, as a noun, means the present era, as in the world of today.
